thread:
erin: Heads-up — nightly perf CI didn't produce nsys .qdrep traces for the new KV eviction kernel on dedicated-A. CI logs show nvprof logs but no .qdrep in the S3 artifact bundle. Anyone else seeing missing traces?

erin: snippet from the runner logs:
```
[run 2026-03-17T03:12:01Z] nsys: starting sampling (min-runtime=0.05s)
[run 2026-03-17T03:12:06Z] profiler: completed, uploaded artifacts (no qdrep found)
```

trace-bot: nightly-perf-job-2026-03-17 completed; artifacts uploaded to s3://ci-perf-artifacts/nightly/2026-03-17/ (note: qdrep not present for runner dedicated-A).

sam: I saw this on a separate run. I think the sampler threshold is too aggressive — small kernels finish before we warm up. We should lower `--min-runtime` for the nightly capture or add an explicit forced capture for kernels matching `kv_*`.

chris: What is our current sampler config in perf-ci.yaml? IIRC we set `min_runtime: 0.05` and `sample_window_ms: 20`. For nsys good CUDA api stacks we need larger windows (>=50ms) or repeated invocations. We could add a PR-only smoke stage that runs a longer single trace.

chris: example change (draft):
```yaml
stages:
  - name: perf-smoke-pr
    when: paths_changed: ["runtime/kv/**"]
    steps:
      - run: ./ci/perf_run.sh --nsys --force-capture --duration 5s
```

erin: timeline analysis on the failing runs shows the eviction kernel occupied ~12ms per invocation and got batched out — so sampling rarely hit it. For nightly we could lower the threshold or bump the warmup to capture more tiny events. Nightly cost is acceptable; PRs are the expensive vector.

marie: We can add a cheap 5s smoke-run stage on PRs but gate it to only run when the PR touches runtime/kv or the scheduler. That keeps cost down and gives deterministic traces for small kernels.

tj: Concern: extra GPU minutes across all PRs. Alternative: run smoke only on the first PR in a stack or on labeled runs (`perf/trace-request`). Also we could run the smoke on a smaller instance type to reduce cost.

sam: Another angle — post-process traces and generate a small `kernel-fingerprint.json` for each artifact (hash of kernel name + input-shape + grid/block). Store that alongside artifacts so the diff dashboard can match kernels even when the qdrep filename is missing.

erin: Good idea. Action plan I'm proposing: (1) add forced smoke-stage for PRs that touch `runtime/kv` (5s duration), (2) lower nightly sampler `min_runtime` from 50ms to 20ms just for nightly, (3) emit `kernel-fingerprint.json` metadata with each trace upload. Anyone object?

chris: :thumbsup: No objections. I can get a PR ready tonight and target the nightly run tomorrow.

trace-bot: Created PERF-3142: "CI: ensure nsys qdrep + kernel fingerprinting for kv eviction path" (https://issues.redwood.ai/PERF-3142).

marie: I'll add a post-processor that picks up the qdrep/qdxml (if present) and writes `kernel-fingerprint.json` + `summary.json` and uploads both to S3 with the artifact. Also will update the perf-diff DB ingestion to index the fingerprint. Need an S3 ACL tweak (short-lived put tokens).

erin: Thanks — action owners: @chris PR for perf-ci, @marie post-processor & perf-diff ingestion, @sam verify sampler flags and add unit test for min-runtime heuristics, @tj run cost estimate. I'll monitor tomorrow's nightly and post results here. :eyes:

sam: quick check command we can use in CI to decide whether to force-capture: `git diff --name-only $PR_BASE $PR_HEAD | grep -E "runtime/kv|runtime/scheduler"` — only run smoke if match.

chris: I'll include that in the CI step. Also adding a tiny lint that fails PR if someone changes low-level kernel code without a perf smoke or a note — prevents silent regressions.

erin: Perfect. If anyone hits blocking items while implementing, ping here or DM. Thanks! :raised_hands:
